analysis.title: Network Thoughts: Strong Q3 Earnings Overwhelmed By Positioning Unwind
key_insights: Q3 earnings are strong but are being overwhelmed by hedge fund positioning unwinds. About 25% of S&P market cap has reported, 78% of companies beat expectations, revenue is growing 12.5% and earnings are tracking 31% higher y/y. Every sector shows positive growth, but only Energy and Technology outpace S&P growth.

Hedge funds are selling AI Winners and Momentum. The derisking is comparable to July and has been overshadowed by a surge in short exposure. Since September, long exposure fell from the 90th to the 15th percentile and shorts rose from the 15th to the 80th percentile. Nets are at the 25th percentile.

UBS Knowledge Network estimates equity long/short strategies are down 7% in October so far, and quant funds are flat. US discretionary equity hedge funds are down 6.7% this month, and the last two days cost quants all their monthly gains.

Flows were supportive despite the unwind. On Thursday there was $52bn of excess S&P buy flow and $25bn of excess Nasdaq sell flow, mostly from systematic funds. UBS retail market making bought the dip for the fifth time this month, mostly in ETFs, Tech and Semiconductors.

UBS US equity strategist Keith Parker lists possible circuit breakers: hyperscaler cloud beats, no Fed hike with less hawkish rhetoric, Iran and oil developments, and buybacks. He prefers names with higher growth and CFROI that trade at a discount (UBEQHGCD).

Equity index implied volatility is rising after staying calm through the September bond-market disruption. The VIX broke back above 20 this week and the VSTOXX hit a five-month high. Index vol is rising faster than single-stock vol, which lifts implied correlation after extreme de-correlation in the first three quarters.

Put-wing skews are re-steepening and hedging interest is picking up, with traded notional in S&P puts at an all-time high. The US index is less than 2% from all-time highs, and UBS suggests put spreads for investors hedging a break lower into year-end.

Within AI, long selling of semiconductors drove this month's degrossing, but the past two days were long selling of hyperscalers on capex overspending concerns. Buyers are returning to semiconductors, memory and hardware, while heavier shorting within AI Winners shows reluctance to reload on AI beta.

European positioning is prone to a squeeze. Short exposure has been near the 100th percentile (five-year) for much of the year, long exposure is below the 5th percentile, and gross exposure is above the 90th percentile. European equity long/short funds are down 2.8% for the month.
Japan de-grossing is broader, with 3.5% net outflows this week and Tech the most sold sector. Tech is about 35% of Japan net exposure. Japan equity long/short funds are down 8.2% for the month.

French budget fears pushed the 10y yield up about 20bp this week (up to 34bp at one point). The OAT-Bund spread widened as much as 40bp and OATs yielded more than 100bp over Spain. Parliament has amended, deleted or rejected key articles of PM Lecornu's budget.

More than €4bn of planned French budget improvements were discarded by late week, likely more than €10bn once social security rejections come. The deficit is likely to stay unchanged rather than fall from 5.4% to 5.0% of GDP. The worst case is rolling over the 2026 budget, which probably lacks enough cuts to satisfy markets.

French growth cannot support higher OAT yields. Trend growth is about 1.0% or less, 2026 GDP is likely 0.5%, and the 10y OAT real yield is 3.20%, about 220bp higher. Spain's 10y real rate is 1.90% against potential growth near 2.0%. The ECB is expected to raise its deposit rate in mid-December and again next spring to 3.00%, which UBS says suits Spain (inflation 5%) but hurts France (inflation 3%).
The UBS French Domestics basket (UBXEFREX) is down 3.5% this week against the CAC down 2.5%, consistent with Knowledge Network's earlier link between rising OAT yields and the basket's decline.

UBS sees the APAC tech sell-off as a low-volume confidence shock, not a fundamental break. Positioning was less stretched than in the summer unwind and fundamental deterioration is limited beyond AI financing and data-centre investment concerns. APAC long/short funds are down 8.0% and Japan down 8.7% in October per UBS prime brokerage.

Korea and China could provide the bid. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix report next week. UBS estimates Samsung FCF yield at 22% for 2026 and 35% for 2027, and SK Hynix at 20% and 34%. Higher shareholder returns could bring investors back. China's National Team has been a steady buyer since mid-October and was widely credited for Friday's 7% intraday swing recovery.

EM FX implied volatility spiked to levels last seen in March, driven by LatAm: election-related BRL volatility and a long MXN unwind after a dovish Banxico pivot. Short USDMXN is crowded but has room to rise given legacy MXN longs and CTA signals flipping long.

UBS expects G10 FX volatility to rise into the central bank wave: RBNZ Oct 27, FOMC and BoC Oct 28, ECB Oct 29, BoJ Oct 30. G10 1m and 3m implied vols are both 6.7, below the roughly 8.1 five-year average, and the ATM vol curve is flat despite Q4 catalysts including the UK fiscal budget, OAT stress and US midterm elections.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 earnings are strong: 78% beat, revenue +12.5%, earnings +31% y/y, retail and systematic flows supportive, and the index is within 2% of all-time highs. Possible circuit breakers are hyperscaler cloud beats, no Fed hike, Iran and oil developments, and buybacks.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds are cutting longs and adding shorts, long/short funds are losing money, volatility and put hedging are rising, and hyperscaler capex worries are driving long selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler cloud beats, no Fed hike with less hawkish rhetoric, and buybacks would stop the unwind. A hawkish Fed would extend it.

tension_points.bull_case: The sell-off looks like a low-volume confidence shock. Korean cash returns and China's National Team buying could provide a bid, and Samsung and SK Hynix FCF yields are very high.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds remain reluctant to re-engage after repeated P&L reversals, thin liquidity amplifies declines, and AI financing and data-centre investment concerns persist.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Samsung and SK Hynix reporting next week without raising shareholder returns would remove the Korean catalyst.
